description: Our team focuses on harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS satellite data to improve consistency, accuracy, and reliability. We work on integrating observations from both sensors to support environmental monitoring, vegetation analysis, land surface studies, and long-term climate research.
summary: Burning Activity Explorer is an interactive web tool that makes NASA's two main satellite fire-detection systems, MODIS and VIIRS, comparable on one map. We loaded the 2025 NASA FIRMS archive (five satellites, four data files) and built a harmonization pipeline: one common data schema, one display scale for detection confidence, one clock (UTC converted to IST), and flagged cross-sensor matches within 1 km and 3 hours. Users can filter by sensor, date and confidence, click any point or any location to see its detections, explore an activity calendar, replay the season day by day, and compare the two sensors. The comparison shows that although VIIRS reports far more detections because of its smaller pixels, the weekly pattern of activity agrees closely (correlation 0.93). This matters because forest-fire monitoring depends on combining several satellites, and raw counts from different sensors can mislead. We label every marker a hotspot detection, not a confirmed fire, and the data as a historical archive.
details:
Overview: Burning Fire Explorer is a 17-module interactive platform that harmonizes active fire detections from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS sensors into one consistent, explorable dataset. It turns two mismatched satellite sources into a single, trustworthy view of global fire activity.

How it works: MODIS (about 1 km resolution) and VIIRS (about 375 m resolution) detect fires differently, so we align their formats, timestamps, locations and confidence levels. Users can then explore the unified data through:

  • 3D Global Map, Regional Explorer and Hotspot Intelligence to see where fires are burning and which areas are persistent hotspots
  • Sensor Comparison and Cross-Sensor Matches to see how MODIS and VIIRS agree or differ on the same fire events
  • Analytics, Time Intelligence and Activity Calendar to study trends, seasonal patterns and daily activity
  • Data Explorer and Data Quality to filter raw detections and check reliability
  • Investigation Lab, Investigation Reports and Research Studio for deeper, report-ready analysis
  • Scientific Intelligence and Environmental & AI Lab for advanced scientific and AI-driven insights
  • Methodology for full transparency on how harmonization was done

Benefits: Researchers, forest departments, disaster response teams and the public get one clear picture of fire activity instead of juggling two incompatible datasets. It also keeps long-term fire records consistent as older MODIS satellites are replaced by VIIRS.

Impact: Better fire monitoring supports faster response, smarter resource planning and a deeper understanding of how fire patterns are changing.

Tools used: Python, NASA FIRMS, HTML, Javascript

Creativity: Rather than treating each sensor separately, we bridge them and wrap the result in a full research workspace, from a 3D globe to investigation reports, so a non-technical user and a scientist can both use it.

Factors considered: Resolution differences, detection confidence, duplicate detections, data quality, transparency of method and ease of use.
